issues.description: Constructor parameter order for class Lecture is ambiguous: the problem text (problem_statement.md lines 16-17) lists attributes in the order: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors. The UML diagram in the same problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 63-69) presents attributes in a different order (numberOfInscribedStudents appears before lectureName and numberOfLecturers appears before numberOfGuestStudents). The reference implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) declares the constructor signature with parameters in the order: (String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) which matches the textual list but not the UML. This discrepancy can confuse students about the expected constructor parameter order and may cause test mismatches if a specific signature is enforced.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected constructor signature unambiguous: update the UML diagram in problem_statement.md to list attributes in the same order as the textual description and the solution constructor (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), or explicitly state the exact constructor signature in the problem text (e.g. public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors)). Ensure template and tests (if any) use the same signature.
